title: Temperature-change links to corrected trawl community change were uncertain in four US samples in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested whether larger annual changes in seasonal sea-surface temperature went with larger changes in recorded community composition. We used eastern Bering Sea and Northeast US fall trawl records in 1982-2019. One haul per fixed stratum defines each taxon detection probability. We subtract a finite-sample term from squared changes in these probabilities. Under independent haul sampling within strata, the corrected measure is unbiased for squared change in the underlying probabilities. Four region-period models control linear year. All four adjusted slope intervals include zero. Slopes are 1.04 and -0.48 in early and late Bering samples, and 2.32 and -5.16 in early and late Northeast samples. Covariance and survey-transition checks retain the uncertain result. Mean subtracted terms are 20-69 percent of mean direct distances. This shows the size of the correction, not measured field error. Short series, spatial sampling, gear, detection and coarse surface temperature limit inference. We do not estimate causal climate effects or test pollution. The package gives code, sufficient data, raw provenance, a figure and independent numerical checks.

display.caption: Annual community change at fixed haul effort and temperature-change slopes in four region-period samples. All four adjusted intervals include zero. The upper panels show raw pair values; the lower panels control linear midpoint year.

citations.reason: Reuse verified published incidence counts, haul denominators, seasonal SST panel, raw provenance and source build code. We test community probability distance and temperature changes rather than richness and temperature levels. Raw observations overlap.
Prior marine heatwave and fish community study motivates this distinct seasonal-change test. This is not an independent replication of its heatwave target.
Prior assessment of trawl availability and sampling limits.
